jesse.sales: Heads-up — Acme (large fintech) wants a short POC for BYOK via HSM. They need: no internet egress from KMS proxy, rotation every 90d, audit log forwarding to their Splunk, and an option for Dedicated vs Private deployment. Can we confirm the preflight checklist and cost delta?
ana.solutions: @jesse.sales thanks. quick clarifying q: do they require customer key escrow (two-custodian ceremony) or are they okay with Redwood acting as key-wrapping proxy?
jesse.sales: Riley on their side said they want full customer control (no Redwood escrows) and the key material must never leave the HSM. They prefer CloudHSM-compatible flow but are open to a Thales-style model if needed.
ben.crypto: We support two common BYOK flows: 1) Bring-your-own-key (wrapped CMK import via HSM vendor APIs) and 2) Remote unwrap where customer signs an import request and we call the vendor API. For strict "never leaves HSM" we need the customer to provision the key directly into their HSM and expose a PKCS#11 endpoint or a KMS proxy we can route to.
riley.acme: Confirmed — we'll provision our HSM and give a private endpoint reachable from Redwood in the VPC peering path. No public IPs. Also need rotation to be orchestrated by us, but Redwood needs to support step-change (rebind) without downtime.
ana.solutions: Ok — networking checklist we'll need from the customer: allowed IP blocks, DNS name for the proxy, mTLS cert for service account, and test endpoint. Also need expected QPS/latency (p99 requirement).
jesse.sales: They said p95 for key ops ~80ms and p99 under 200ms. Volume is modest — ~50 KMS ops/sec peak across the org.
ben.crypto: 50 ops/sec is small. Two operational notes: 1) Continuous caching of decrypted prefixes isn't applicable to KMS calls; we rely on fast HSM path. 2) For rotation with zero-downtime we provide a dual-write canary: both old and new keys accepted for a short window; customer must support a transition mode on their side.
riley.acme: That dual-write approach is acceptable. We need the rotation playbook written into the SOW — including rollback steps and a disaster recovery key-escrow path (only invoked under legal request).
legal-bot: Heads-up: engineering/legal will need to review the SOW clause for "escrow only under court order" language. Also confirm whether key rotation cadence <90d has any contractual ops surcharge.
finance.ops: FYI — BYOK with private HSM proxy has an onboarding fee (one-time) and a monthly private deployment premium. I'll draft a simple pricing delta for Dedicated vs Private by EOD.
ana.solutions: For preflight, provide the customer this quick connectivity test to verify inbound peering and TLS:
```bash
# run from customer's bastion to our proposed proxy
openssl s_client -connect kms-proxy.redwood-internal:443 -servername kms.acme.internal -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/acme-root.pem
# or a basic port check
nc -vz kms-proxy.redwood-internal 443
```
ben.crypto: Also collect PKCS#11 module version (if using HSM vendor) and supported key types (RSA2048/RSA3072/ECC). We'll need the vendor's import API docs.
jesse.sales: Action items: 1) @ana.solutions write SOW draft with rotation playbook & rollback. 2) @ben.crypto list supported PKCS#11 vendors and exact latency expectations. 3) @finance.ops send price delta (onboarding + monthly premium). 4) Riley to send IP ranges, bastion test access window, and vendor import docs.
riley.acme: I'll send the network ranges and schedule a 1-hr kickoff for Friday 10am PT. Also attaching vendor docs in the next message.
deploy-bot: Runbook created: /runbooks/sales/acme-byok-poc — includes checklist, test commands, and contact matrix. :white_check_mark:
nana.solutions: I'll put the SOW draft in the runbook and ping legal for wording. If we can get the network test results before Friday we can avoid a second preflight.
jesse.sales: Great — let's aim for Friday. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
